key_insight: Paid promotional articles on user-generated-content platforms can become source material for AI-generated answers. GEOHunter examines one such generative engine optimization (GEO) operation across three major Chinese platforms; the supplied abstract does not include its results.
problem_solved: Investigating how paid-content operations seek visibility in generative engines, with particular concern for misleading medical and financial advice.
method: Study a paid GEO operation that publishes promotional articles for clients.
Measure the operation across three major Chinese user-generated-content platforms.
Examine the concern that promotional web content may influence AI-generated answers, recommendations, and rankings.
impact: The study highlights a source-integrity risk for retrieval-based AI: promotional content may shape answers without users recognizing its commercial origin. This motivates stronger provenance tracking and evaluation of promotional influence, especially in high-stakes domains.
visual_elements: Flow diagram: paying client → GEO service → promotional UGC articles → generative engine → user answer.
Network schematic connecting one GEO operation with three UGC platforms.
Medical and financial icons highlighting high-stakes misinformation risks.
Side-by-side illustration of an independent source and a paid promotional article entering retrieval.
paper_title: GEOHunter: Mapping a Generative Engine Optimization Network in the Wild
paper_authors: Sean Tang, Peiran Wang, Ying Li, Esha Shivakumar, Tao Meng
